habitat: Wikipedia says it is a non-migratory bird of southern Africa, formerly included in the Long-billed Pipit. The SABAP1 Long-billed Pipit account, written when the two were not separated, places that bird on rocky slopes, singly or in pairs.
summary: No Newman page, and neither Wikipedia nor the SABAP1 Long-billed Pipit text gives a plumage description that can be separated for this species. Wikipedia says it is non-migratory, so status is resident. No length and no Kruger-box photograph. The Kemp paper name Longbilled Pipit and the code RB were left unchanged.

sources.title: Longbilled Pipit. In Harrison, J.A. et al. (eds). The Atlas of Southern African Birds. Vol. 2.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

calls.description: The sources used do not describe the call. Grade A call from Boskloof, Cape Town, catalogued as Anthus nicholsoni. The filename is XC425855-Pipit Long-billed Boskloof170718.mp3.

research.note: No Newman page. Wikipedia says non-migratory and gives no plumage or total length. The SABAP1 text is the former combined Long-billed Pipit account and does not describe plumage. No openly licensed research-grade photo was found in the Kruger box. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
